text:
ConocoPhillips rose 2.1% today after reporting third-quarter earnings of $4 billion, or $3 per share, on Thursday. The stock had fallen sharply over the previous two trading days—dropping nearly $10 from $146.84 to $136.94—likely in reaction to broader energy sector uncertainty around the midterm elections and mixed signals on global oil demand. Today's gain represents a partial recovery as investors digested the actual earnings results.

The mixed backdrop for energy remains: US oil is trading at $99.64 per barrel while world oil sits at $107.03, reflecting continued geopolitical risk and demand questions that the broader sector is wrestling with. The stock's 4% decline over two weeks shows investors are weighing strong profit against an uncertain outlook for energy demand and policy shifts ahead.
